videos.title: When the Shortest Route Looks Curved #math #Shorts

editorial.opening: Two contrasting routes share endpoints on a map; the curved one prompts the geometric question.
editorial.mechanism: Identical sampled routes move into an oblique sphere projection. A central great circle and radii support the distinction; a Rodrigues rotation carries the same route to a north-pole view.
editorial.readability: A faint spherical grid provides depth. Numeric route lengths and the polar-angle annotation have their own space.
editorial.pacing: The comparison proceeds steadily. The verbal minimal-path argument near the end is more abstract than the opening map observation.
editorial.sound: Dry local narration. Full decode and independent ASR differences reviewed. No subjective listening or claim of pleasing prosody.
editorial.remaining_weaknesses: The globe is transparent linework. The map-to-globe transition is a representation change, while the later reorientation is a genuine rotation. Sideways wandering is not separately animated, so the general lower-bound argument is only partly visual.
